expectations.text: Distinguishes between possible CAUSES of the drop-off before proposing fixes, rather than going straight to an idea list
expectations.evidence: Paragraph 2, before any option: '**First, which 60% is this?** Three buckets that share no fixes: (a) never got the message ... (b) got it, didn't finish ... (c) finished later on another device and your session-scoped funnel logged them as lost. Delivery logs plus a 7-day cohort view separates all three in an afternoon.'

expectations.text: Raises that the 60% may be composed of different populations, or may be partly a measurement or attribution artifact
expectations.evidence: Both halves are covered: the attribution artifact — '(c) finished later on another device and your session-scoped funnel logged them as lost' — and the population point — 'Split by acquisition source too: if the drop concentrates in one paid channel, 60% may be correct sorting rather than a broken step, and none of the below applies.'

expectations.text: Does not re-propose shortening the form or adding a progress bar
expectations.evidence: Neither is proposed; the tried fixes are used as evidence against the friction reading — 'Every one of those is a place to lose them and none of them is the form — which is why shortening it didn't help.' The cut list also retires the adjacent family: 'Better copy, trust badges, reminder drips — same family as the progress bar. You've done that.'

expectations.text: At least one option questions whether verification needs to happen at that point in the flow at all
expectations.evidence: Two do. 'Stop checking most people, and price what leaks through ... If the premium exceeds the claim, let almost everyone through and screen against known-bad after the fact.' And 'Deliver the thing before there's an account to verify ... The check stops being an admission ticket and becomes a save button.'

expectations.text: Options differ in mechanism (channel, timing, who verifies, whether to verify) rather than in copy, layout, or visual design
expectations.evidence: Six options on six different axes: whether to verify at all (price the abuse); whether an account exists yet (stateless session); what is being verified (splitting reachability / uniqueness / legal identity, each fired at a different moment); what evidence is used (passkey, OAuth session, employer domain, card on file — 'background classification over those signals rather than an interactive event'); removal of the cross-app handoff (server-side polling, reply-as-proof); and a human intervention ('Treat every stall as an inbound lead, for two weeks'). No copy or layout suggestion appears.

expectations.text: Handles the ambiguity in 'account-verification' — either asks which kind, or states which reading it assumed and what would change under the others
expectations.evidence: Line 1: 'I'm reading "account verification" as a confirmation code or link sent to email/SMS. If it's really ID-document upload or bank linking, tell me — options 1 and 2 largely stop applying and 4 becomes most of the answer.' Names the reading and the specific consequence of being wrong.

expectations.text: Proportionate to a bounded product question: under roughly 1200 words, no ceremonial section headings with no content under them
expectations.evidence: wc -w = 1136, under the 1200 ceiling. Every heading carries a mechanism plus three substantive lines (what has to be true / failure mode / who runs it). Noted as the weakest pass in the set: it is 330 words longer than the baseline (806) and 146 longer than iteration 3's with_skill run (990) for the same bounded question.

expectations.text: MODE CHECK: did NOT run a full deep multi-agent pass with parallel generators and web research on this bounded problem
expectations.evidence: user_notes.md line 1: 'MODE: fast'. metrics.json: subagents_spawned = 0, web_searches = 0, total_tool_calls = 8. The gate table in user_notes records 1 of 5 conditions holding and correctly refuses to let 'the user is stuck' alone trigger deep.

expectations.text: The diagnosis block is a signpost rather than a section: roughly 3 lines or under ~120 words, not a third of the response
expectations.evidence: The diagnosis is a single bolded-lead paragraph of 87 words (7.7% of 1136), with no heading of its own: 'First, which 60% is this? Three buckets ... Delivery logs plus a 7-day cohort view separates all three in an afternoon.' Iteration 3's fast-mode diagnosis ran ~170 words as a headed block.

expectations.text: Does not quote a diversity score or any other internal process metric to the reader
expectations.evidence: No score, lens name, cluster, phase or pass count appears in response.md. user_notes.md records that the script returned '17.70 effectively distinct (98%)' and that this was deliberately kept out of the deliverable.
